Reviewed complete meta.anchors.content.blocks claim and both ordinary associations: spec.rs implementation and claims_retain_all_blocks_until_the_next_definition_or_document_end test. Content must begin after the marker, preserve every intervening Markdown block and internal blank line, and stop at the first applicable boundary. parse_anchors starts content at code_range.end, keeps active across paragraph/list/table/code events, and finalizes at a following valid marker, heading, explicit end or input end. finish_anchor slices the entire original extent and trims only exterior whitespace. The associated test asserts exact first content containing Unicode, multiple paragraphs, blank lines, a list, table, fenced code, indented code and quotation; exact second content retains its final paragraph through document end. Both source-span slices equal content and first content ends before the next marker. These assertions would detect dropped blocks, premature blank-line termination, included markers or merged adjacent claims. Specific heading/explicit-end rules have separate anchors; the current test meaningfully checks this block-preservation claim at next-definition and document boundaries. Captured source helper simply constructs SpecSource without rewriting text. No TODO/N/A evidence or deferred prerequisites exist.
